interests.title: Interests
interests.blurb: Swipe through activities and tell us what you enjoy.
interests.intro: You'll see a stack of everyday activities. For each one, show how much you'd enjoy doing it. There are no right or wrong answers, just what feels like you.
interests.how: Swipe left for dislike, right for like, up for love. Or tap the buttons under the card.

personality.title: Personality
personality.blurb: Say how well short statements describe you.
personality.intro: These are short statements about how you usually think, feel and act. Pick the answer that fits you best, not the one that sounds best.
personality.how: Choose one of five answers for each statement. You can go back to change an answer.

values.title: Values
values.blurb: Sort what matters to you in a future job.
values.intro: You'll see things people want from work, like good pay or a calm workplace. Sort them by how much they matter to you.
values.how: Put each card in a group. Only 7 can be "must have", so choose carefully. Then pick your top 3 values.

abilities.title: Strengths
abilities.blurb: Rate how strong you feel in different skills.
abilities.intro: Rate yourself on a few skills compared with others your age. This is how you see yourself, so be honest and kind to yourself.
abilities.how: Choose one of five answers for each skill. These are self-reported strengths, not a test.

context.title: About you
context.blurb: A few quick questions about your studies and plans.
context.intro: A few quick questions help us suggest paths that fit your studies and situation. Skip any you'd rather not answer.
context.how: Everything here is optional and saves as you go.

how.1: Answer honestly. There are no right or wrong answers.
how.2: Your answers are saved as you go. You can pause and come back any time.
how.3: At the end you'll see careers that fit you. No scores show up until then.

prompts.personality: How well does this describe you?
prompts.abilities: Compared with others your age, how strong are you at this?

swipe.help: Swipe left: {left}. Swipe right: {right}. Swipe up: {up}. Or use the buttons or the arrow keys.

lines.0: Nice pace. There are no right or wrong answers here.
lines.1: Go with your first instinct. It's usually the most honest one.
lines.2: Remember, you can pause and come back any time.
lines.3: Answer for who you are today, not who you think you should be.
lines.4: Every answer helps paint a fuller picture of you.
lines.5: Take a breath if you need one. There's no timer.

R.name: Hands-on
R.meaning: You like practical work: building, fixing, using tools, being active and seeing something real at the end.
R.shows: You would rather try it than read about it, and you feel at home with machines, nature or physical tasks.

I.name: Investigative
I.meaning: You like to figure things out: asking why, analysing information and solving hard problems.
I.shows: You enjoy puzzles, experiments and deep questions, and you are happy to spend time on one problem until it clicks.

A.name: Creative
A.meaning: You like to express ideas: designing, writing, making and imagining things that did not exist before.
A.shows: You notice style and detail, you like freedom in how you work, and you often have a different angle.

S.name: Helping
S.meaning: You like working with people: teaching, caring, listening and making a difference to someone's day.
S.shows: Friends come to you to talk, and you feel energised when you help someone understand or feel better.

E.name: Leading
E.meaning: You like to lead and persuade: starting projects, taking decisions and moving people towards a goal.
E.shows: You speak up, take initiative and enjoy the challenge of convincing others or building something of your own.

C.name: Organising
C.meaning: You like order and detail: planning, keeping records accurate and making systems run smoothly.
C.shows: You like clear steps and checklists, you spot mistakes quickly, and people rely on you to get things right.

extraversion.name: Energy around people
extraversion.meaning: How much you draw energy from talking, teamwork and being in the middle of things.
extraversion.shows: Higher bands show up as an easy start to conversations and a love of group work. Calmer bands show up as focus, listening and thoughtful one-to-one time.

agreeableness.name: Care and cooperation
agreeableness.meaning: How naturally you look out for others, work as a team and keep the peace.
agreeableness.shows: You notice how people feel, you share credit, and groups work better with you in them.

conscientiousness.name: Organisation and reliability
conscientiousness.meaning: How much you plan ahead, follow through and take care with your work.
conscientiousness.shows: Deadlines, tidy notes and finishing what you start. This is one of the strongest signals of study and work success.

emotionalStability.name: Calm under pressure
emotionalStability.meaning: How steady you stay when things get stressful, like exams, surprises or criticism.
emotionalStability.shows: You recover quickly after a setback and can keep thinking clearly when others are rushing.

intellect.name: Curiosity and ideas
intellect.meaning: How much you enjoy new ideas, learning and looking at things in unusual ways.
intellect.shows: You ask follow-up questions, enjoy trying new methods and get bored when everything stays the same.

achievement.name: Achievement
achievement.meaning: Wanting work where you use your abilities and can see your effort turn into results.
achievement.shows: You are happiest when you can point at what you accomplished.

workingConditions.name: Stable conditions
workingConditions.meaning: Wanting a secure, comfortable workplace with a steady routine and fair pay.
workingConditions.shows: You value knowing what to expect and having a life outside work.

recognition.name: Recognition
recognition.meaning: Wanting your good work to be noticed and to move up over time.
recognition.shows: You are motivated by progress, titles and being respected for your skill.

relationships.name: Good relationships
relationships.meaning: Wanting friendly colleagues and work that helps other people.
relationships.shows: The people around you shape how much you enjoy a job.

support.name: Supportive place
support.meaning: Wanting managers who back you and a workplace that treats people fairly.
support.shows: You do your best when you feel trusted and can ask for help.

independence.name: Independence
independence.meaning: Wanting freedom to decide how you do your work, with little supervision.
independence.shows: You like owning your approach and trying your own ideas.

verbal.name: Words and language
verbal.meaning: Understanding, explaining and writing ideas clearly.
verbal.shows: Reading, discussions, presentations and learning languages tend to come easily.

numerical.name: Numbers
numerical.meaning: Working comfortably with figures, percentages and calculations.
numerical.shows: You estimate quickly, enjoy patterns in data and are comfortable with maths.

logical.name: Logic and reasoning
logical.meaning: Spotting patterns, following rules and working out what comes next.
logical.shows: You enjoy puzzles, step-by-step problem solving and finding the flaw in an argument.

spatial.name: Shapes and space
spatial.meaning: Picturing objects, maps and layouts in your head and turning them around.
spatial.shows: Diagrams, building things, design and finding your way around come naturally.

creative.name: Creative thinking
creative.meaning: Coming up with many original ideas and new ways to solve problems.
creative.shows: You brainstorm freely and connect ideas other people keep separate.

manual.name: Hands and coordination
manual.meaning: Working accurately with your hands and tools.
manual.shows: Fixing, crafting, drawing or handling equipment feels natural and precise.

landing.metaDescription: A science-based journey for Egyptian students aged 15–18: understand yourself, see the careers that fit, and plan your next steps.
landing.headline: Find your world.
landing.subhead: Understand what you enjoy and what you’re good at, see the careers that fit you, and plan your next steps in Egypt — in about 40 minutes.
landing.proof1: Built on validated science (O*NET, Big Five)
landing.heroAlt: An example world: a path through a landscape shaped by someone’s interests.

discover.title: Discover
discover.body: Four short stations about your interests, how you work, what matters to you and your strengths.

match.title: Match
match.body: See careers ranked by how well they fit you — and why, in plain words.

act.title: Act
act.body: Explore Egyptian universities, programs and courses, then build your roadmap.

landing.parentsBody: See your child’s strengths and career areas, and get a guide for talking about them — without seeing their private answers.
landing.schoolsBody: Join our free pilot: your students get guidance, and your counselors get an anonymous group report.

science.a: anaBokra uses established questionnaires (O*NET interests, the IPIP Big Five) that are being adapted and validated with Egyptian students. Results are guidance, not a diagnosis.

time.a: About 40 minutes, split into four short stations you can pause and resume.

privacy.a: Only you. Parents and schools see summaries, never your answers. You can download or delete your data.

parents.q: Do I need my parents’ permission?
parents.a: If you are under 18, a parent or guardian confirms by WhatsApp before your full assessment starts.

start.metaTitle: anaBokra — find the career that fits you
start.metaDescription: Short, fun tasks show what you enjoy and what you're good at. Then check the career paths that suit you. Free, no account, on your phone.
start.headline: Find the career that fits you.
start.subhead: Short, fun tasks show what you enjoy and what you're good at. Then check the paths that suit you and the careers inside them.
start.ctaHint: Free · no account · on your phone
start.heroAlt: An example world: a path through a landscape shaped by someone’s interests.

discover.title: Discover
discover.body: Ten short tasks on your own island, a minute or two each, about what you enjoy, your strengths and how you work.

verify.title: Check a path
verify.body: The career groups closest to you light up. Try a group's tasks to see whether it really fits you, and why.

careers.title: See the careers
careers.body: Read what each career is like in Egypt: the work itself, the study that leads to it and the job market.

time.a: Each task takes a minute or two. Do one, stop, and come back whenever you like. Your answers are saved as you go.

privacy.a: Only you. Your answers and results stay on your phone, encrypted. There's no account, and nothing personal is sent to anaBokra.

who.a: Anyone aged 15 to 25 who is thinking about what to study or which career to aim for.

science.a: We use established questionnaires (O*NET interests and IPIP personality traits) that we are adapting and testing with young Egyptians. Results are guidance, not a diagnosis.

teaser.metaDescription: 12 quick questions to preview your interest profile.
teaser.introBody: {n} quick cards, about 3 minutes. Swipe right for “like”, left for “dislike”, or up for “love”.
teaser.privacy: No account needed. Your answers stay on this device until you choose to save them.
teaser.swipeHint: Swipe the card, or tap an answer.
teaser.resultIntro: Based on 12 quick answers. The full assessment gives you a complete picture.

types.R: You enjoy hands-on, practical work: building, fixing and working with tools or nature.
types.I: You enjoy investigating: asking why, experimenting and solving problems.
types.A: You enjoy creating: ideas, design, writing, music and self-expression.
types.S: You enjoy helping people: teaching, caring and supporting others.
types.E: You enjoy leading: persuading, organizing people and starting things.
types.C: You enjoy organizing: details, data, order and doing things accurately.

teaser.lockedWorld: Your full world unlocks after 4 stations.
teaser.tourCareers: Careers ranked by how well they fit you, with reasons.
teaser.tourOpportunities: Universities, programs and courses in Egypt.
teaser.disclaimer: This preview is guidance, not a diagnosis.

parents.title: anaBokra for parents
parents.intro: Help your child make a confident, informed choice about their studies and career — with science-based guidance and Egyptian data.
parents.scienceBody: Your child answers validated questionnaires about interests, personality, values and strengths. anaBokra matches them with careers and explains why, then shows real study routes in Egypt.

parents.consentBody: For students under 18, a parent or guardian gives consent before the full assessment. You can create a family account and add your child, or confirm a WhatsApp link your child sends you. You can withdraw consent at any time.
parents.disclaimer: anaBokra offers guidance, not a psychological diagnosis.

research.title: Help us check the Arabic questions? (optional)
research.p1: In addition to the anonymous statistics, your individual answers are sent without your name or any ID, with only the session code, your age group, stage and language.
research.p2: Your readiness answers before and after are linked by a random code made on your phone, so we can see how much they change.
research.p3: We delete this data once the research is done, by 17 June 2027 at the latest. Results are published only as group statistics.
research.p4: Saying no changes nothing in the app.
research.settingOn: You’re sharing research data with this session.
research.stopped: Stopped. The readiness answers sent from this phone were deleted. Your other answers were sent without any key, so they can’t be picked out; they are deleted with the rest of the research data by 17 June 2027.
research.stoppedNone: Stopped. Nothing more will be sent. Answers already sent carry no key, so they can’t be picked out; they are deleted with the rest of the research data by 17 June 2027.
research.deleteFailed: Stopped, but we couldn’t reach anaBokra to delete the readiness answers sent from this phone. Try again when you’re online.

pattern.title: Pattern logic
pattern.how: Each row of shapes follows a rule. Work out the rule and pick the shape that fits the empty square.
pattern.calm: Take your time: there's no clock. It starts easy and gets harder.
pattern.gridLabel: A grid of shapes with the last square missing
pattern.wrong: Not quite. The one in green fits.
pattern.explain: Look across each row: something changes the same way every time. Check everything: how many, which shape, the colour and the fill.
